product.summary: Invoicing for freelancers: send invoices, chase late payments, see who owes money.

source.quote: Ledgerly lets freelancers send invoices, chase late payments and see who owes them money.
We launched fourteen months ago.

evidence.value: Revenue around $2,700 a month, growing slowly but steadily

source.quote: Revenue is around $2,700 a month, growing slowly but steadily.
Today we have 140 paying customers on our $19-a-month plan

evidence.value: about 600 more on the free tier

source.quote: about 600 more on the free tier
The current app is a single Rails app on one rented server that I set up myself.
The current app is a single Rails app

availability.value: No written uptime promise; customers expect it up when they bill, at month end

source.quote: Customers do not have a written uptime promise, but they expect the app to be up when they bill

data_loss_tolerance.value: A sent invoice must not be lost; a day of draft edits may be

source.quote: I would rather lose a day of draft edits than a single sent invoice.

data_categories.value: customers' names, emails and business addresses; their clients' names and emails; invoice amounts

source.quote: We store our customers' names, emails, business addresses, their clients' names and emails, and the invoice amounts.

source.why: Contact details of freelancers and their clients plus what each is paid: personal and financial, but no card data, which stays with Stripe.

unknowns.question: Will the accounting firm put 300 of its clients on Ledgerly next year?
unknowns.why_it_matters: Nothing is signed; if it happens, customers and the month-end peak grow several times over.
decisions_affected: tenant model for a firm with many clients

unknowns.question: How much downtime is acceptable at month end, and how fast must the app recover?
unknowns.why_it_matters: There is no written uptime promise, yet staying up at month end is the top priority; the target sets how much redundancy to pay for.

unknowns.question: Does the app need any speed target?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is named; the month-end worry is staying up, so no option turns on speed.

unknowns.question: Has the app faced any named threat or incident?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is named, and card data never reaches the app.

unknowns.question: Does any certification or audit apply?
unknowns.why_it_matters: None is asked for; card rules stay with Stripe.

assumptions.text: Card data stays out of scope by keeping Stripe Checkout as the only card path.
assumptions.why: The brief says card numbers are never seen or stored and must stay with Stripe.
